Reference / fs/temp

fs/temp#

Temporary resources are created eagerly with unpredictable names inside an explicitly supplied directory.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let temporary = TemporaryFile(directory: scratch, prefix: "upload-");
defer temporary.close();
temporary.write(payload);
temporary.flush();
let path is Path = temporary.path();

Description#

Temporary resources are created eagerly with unpredictable names inside an explicitly supplied directory. prefix is one filename component, not a path. Temporary files are binary read/write streams with owner-only permissions:

close() is idempotent and deletes an unpreserved temporary file. Preserve a completed file under a deliberate destination before the deferred close:

let preservation = TemporaryFilePreservation(
    origin: temporary,
    destination: output,
);
preservation.preserve();
let result = preservation.destination();

Preservation never replaces an existing destination. It keeps the operation atomic when both paths share a filesystem and copies in bounded chunks when crossing filesystems.

replace(destination) is the other way to keep it: it takes the place of whatever is at destination in one step, and is never copied. Make the temporary file in the destination's directory, so both share a filesystem:

let temporary = TemporaryFile(directory: Directory(path: output.parent()), prefix: ".report-");
defer temporary.close();
temporary.write(payload);
temporary.replace(output);

It is durable as well as atomic: the file is synchronized before the rename and the directory after it. A reader sees the old file or the new one, never a part. The new file keeps the permission bits of the file it replaces (owner, group and others; through a link, the target's); with nothing there it stays owner-only. It is a new file: hard links to the old one keep the old content, and its owner is whoever runs the program. A symbolic link at destination is itself replaced, and its target is left alone. When the rename was done but the directory could not be synchronized, the new content is in place and the failure is FileError.failed("not_durable", …).

flush() only hands the bytes to the operating system, which may still lose them in a crash; sync() makes them durable, as far as the system and the disk keep that promise.

TemporaryDirectory.close() recursively deletes its contents. Symbolic links are removed as leaves; their targets are never traversed or deleted.

Public API#

object TemporaryFile#

object TemporaryFile does Reading, Writing, WritingText, Closing

A file with an unpredictable name, readable and writable, removed on close unless preserved.

TemporaryFile.TemporaryFile#

TemporaryFile(directory is DirectoryLocating, prefix is string)

Makes the file now inside directory, its name starting with prefix (one name, not a path), readable by the owner only.

TemporaryFile.bytes#

bytes(limit is int) is @byte

At most limit bytes from the current position; [] at the end.

TemporaryFile.write#

write(source is ByteSource) is void

Writes the bytes of source.

TemporaryFile.write#

write(bytes is @byte) is void

Writes the bytes.

TemporaryFile.write#

write(values is ...string) is void

Text, as UTF-8.

TemporaryFile.writeln#

writeln(values is ...string) is void

Writes the strings as UTF-8 and then one LF.

TemporaryFile.flush#

flush() is void

Hands written bytes to the operating system; sync() makes them durable.

TemporaryFile.sync#

sync() is void

Makes written bytes durable: they survive a crash once sync returns, as far as the system and the disk keep that promise (fsync; F_FULLFSYNC on macOS).

TemporaryFile.closed#

closed() is bool

Whether it is closed.

TemporaryFile.close#

close() is void

Closes the file and removes it unless it was preserved.

TemporaryFile.path#

path() is Path

Where it is.

TemporaryFile.size#

size() is int

Its size in bytes on disk now.

TemporaryFile.preserve#

preserve(destination is Path) is void

Keeps the file at destination: renamed when possible, copied across file systems; an existing destination is refused.

TemporaryFile.replace#

replace(destination is Path) is void

Puts the file at destination in one step, replacing what is there, and makes it durable: synchronized, renamed over destination (never copied), then its directory synchronized. It keeps the permission bits of the file it replaces. A failure before the rename leaves destination as it was.

object TemporaryDirectory#

object TemporaryDirectory does DirectoryLocating, Closing

A directory with an unpredictable name, removed with everything in it on close.
